beats.lead: The internet's first ever dot com address did not belong to a tech giant
beats.text: It was symbolics.com, registered on 15 March 1985 by Symbolics Inc, a Massachusetts company that built computers designed specifically to run the Lisp programming language.
beats.note: Symbolics was a spin off from the MIT AI Lab and sold its machines as the best available hardware for artificial intelligence research.

beats.context: How many companies had bothered to register a dot com address by the end of 1985, the format's entire first year.

beats.text: The other five were bbn.com, think.com, mcc.com, dec.com and northrop.com. Symbolics simply moved first.
beats.note: There had been an earlier address, nordu.net, created a few months before, but that identified a network rather than a company registering its own name.

beats.lead: The company that got there first did not last
beats.text: By the late 1980s, cheaper general purpose workstations and new Lisp software for ordinary hardware had erased its advantage, and Symbolics slid into bankruptcy.
beats.note: A former employee later wrote that Symbolics kept believing its own thinking about its hardware even as the market proved it wrong.

beats.text: The record for oldest dot com on the internet is still held by a company most people have never heard of, and it went bankrupt before the web it predates even existed.

beats.line: The internet's first address belonged to an AI company that did not survive the first AI winter.
